title: How to use biblionetwork
text: Co-authorship links authors (institutions, countries) sign documents together. build biblio_coupling(), authors source documents ref, coupling designed : matters count collaboration. coauth_network() offers three ways, optional normalisation productivity authors. see , take toy example: three authors, , b c, sign document 1; b sign document 2. Full counting ("full_counting") gives one point pair authors document co-sign. weight number co-signed documents. –b gets 2 points, –c b–c one point . problem big collaborations weigh : document ten authors creates 45 pairs, adds 45 points network, whereas document two authors adds one. Fractional counting ("fractional_counting") shares value document among co-authors, large collaboration dominate (Perianes-Rodriguez, Waltman, Van Eck 2016). document n authors gives 1/(n-1) pair authors, weights ties author document sum one: author “spends” one unit collaboration per document, split among co-authors. toy example, document 1 three authors, three pairs receives 1/2; document 2 two authors, –b receives 1. weight –b 1/2 + 1 = 1.5, –c b–c 1/2: pair collaborated small team worth pair large team. Perianes-Rodriguez, Waltman, Van Eck (2016) compare full fractional counting bibliometric networks, show choice changes picture. Refined fractional counting ("fractional_counting_refined"), inspired Leydesdorff Park (2017-02), goes one step : document, rather author, total weight one network. document n authors creates n(n-1)/2 pairs, pair gets 2/(n(n-1)). Document 1 gives 1/3 three pairs (3 \times 1/3 = 1) document 2 gives 1 –b. weight –b 1/3 + 1 \approx 1.33. sum weights network number co-authored documents. cases, documents single author ignored, since create tie. Normalising productivity. Prolific authors many collaborations simply publish lot. cosine_normalized = TRUE, weight divided \sqrt{P_i P_j}, P_i number co-authored documents author (Salton’s cosine, coupling angle). weight measures whether two authors collaborate lot relative much collaborates general. toy example, P_a = P_b = 2 P_c = 1: full counting, –b gets 2/\sqrt{2 \times 2} = 1 –c gets 1/\sqrt{2 \times 1} \approx 0.71. stagflation authors, fractional counting cosine normalisation: Note , historical reasons, coauth_network() orients edges Source > Target, opposite functions.
